notes.text: Matthew Robertson has not dressed for the last 11 games. Alberts Šmits has taken his spot beside Braden Schneider. That pair has had 45% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 147:09 together.

Sean Durzi is on injured reserve and has missed the last 3 games. He is a top-four defenseman. Braden Schneider has taken his spot beside Marcus Pettersson. That pair has had 60% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 45:51 together, up from 45% with Durzi.
Luke Glendening was added to the roster on Oct 24 and has played beside Taylor Raddysh and Eeli Tolvanen.
Sean Durzi has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 14 games, up from 7% with his old team last season.

Zach Hyman is on injured reserve (neck injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is a top-six forward. Colton Dach has taken his spot beside Ryan Nugent-Hopkins and Kasperi Kapanen. That line has had 59% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 46:04 together.

Matt Savoie is on long-term injured reserve (lower-body injury) and has not played this season. Leon Draisaitl has taken his spot beside Connor McDavid and Vasily Podkolzin. That line has had 63% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 201:12 together.
Matt Tomkins was added to the roster on Oct 24.
Kasperi Kapanen has started playing on the power play: on the ice for 52% of the team’s power-play time in 17 games, up from 6% last season.
Ty Emberson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 13 games, down from 30% last season.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Oilers won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-1 in New York on Nov 1. The Oilers (11-3-3) lost 5-4 to Anaheim on Thursday, while the Rangers have won two in a row. Going in, the Rangers are third in the Metropolitan (tied for 14th in the NHL) and the Oilers first in the Pacific (tied for third).

The Rangers’ record (.559) is about what their chances are worth. The Oilers’ record (.735) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.591), largely thanks to their finishing. If the Oilers’ record were closer to their chances, like the Rangers’, these teams would be much closer in the standings, so don’t be surprised if this one is closer than the records suggest.

The Oilers (lowest) and the Rangers (2nd lowest) both lean hard on their top players. The Rangers forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd) and get a lot of their shots blocked (32nd). The Oilers have one of the league’s most dangerous power plays (2nd) and get their defensemen shooting (3rd). Edmonton has scored 4.12 goals a game, the most in the league. Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it. Beyond that, both teams play slow, low-event hockey, so expect a tight one.

Adam Fox (2 G / 19 A / 21 P in 17 GP) leads the Rangers in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Alexis Lafrenière (9 G / 7 A / 16 P in 17 GP) has a team-high nine goals. Connor McDavid (10 G / 34 A / 44 P in 17 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with ten points in his last five games and four goals in six games against the Rangers since 2023-24. Leon Draisaitl (14 G / 17 A / 31 P in 17 GP) has a team-high 14 goals, second in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games.
Dylan Garand (6-6-1 / .906 SV% in 11 GS) will likely start for the Rangers, and Matt Tomkins (1-1-0 / .878 SV% in 2 GS) for Edmonton.
